title: The Hi-Hat shows and early 1950s Sixth Ward clubs
summary: Describes the floor shows at the Hi-Hat and other clubs such as Club Desire, the New Pelican and the Gypsy Tea Room.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: It was a photograph of you?
Not with Professor Longhand, but in this club, in that sepia magazine.

Yeah, in the sepia magazine. And they had, well, they had such shows there as they had female impersonator shows and people dancing with snakes and fire. I can remember Maddie Campbell was the snake dancer. Frim Fram was the fire dancer. He put fire and shot it out of the mouth and so forth. Lloyd Ignatius was dancing and so forth. It was a big show that would go on there, you know, and people would come from all over the city to come to this club. It was a black night club in the six bar, where it used to be. Yeah. Yeah. Maddie Campbell. And that was some of our first jobs. And then we'd go down to the club Desire, down in Desire where, what was his name? Henry, I think his name. Old guy used to run the place.

Charlie Armstead. Charlie Armstead. Charlie Armstead. Charlie Armstead. And you know you had Bill Doggett would come down there. And they had the New Pelican uptown, where Count Basie came, the Gypsy Garden, the Gypsy Tea Room, all those kind of places went off, what I'm talking about in the early 50s.
